newsitem.title: USA: US land may be idle even if out of CRP-Farm leader.
newsitem.headline: US land may be idle even if out of CRP-Farm leader.

text.p: U.S. farmers may let some land sit idle when their Conservation Reserver contracts expire next year rather than sow it with crops, the president of the National Association of Wheat Growers said Thursday.

During a panel discussion, NAWG president Chuck Merja said his group was continuing to seek an optional one-year extension of Conservation Reserve contracts that would expire in 1997. Contracts on 24 million acres expire then.
Deputy Agriculture Secretary Richard Rominger said there was no statutory authority to extend contracts.
